title: Customer incident chat-ops and stakeholder templates
author: Marisol Vega
body:
Summary:
This playbook provides ready-to-use chat-ops patterns, channel ownership mappings, incident severity communication templates, and stakeholder briefing message drafts for customer-facing incidents that affect inference quality, availability, or cost. It is intended for Customer Success Engineers (CSEs), Support on-call, Solutions Engineering, and the Incident Commander when coordinating public and private enterprise customers during a live event.

Goals:
- Ensure consistent, fast, and transparent customer communications.
- Reduce cognitive load on responders with pre-approved message templates.
- Clarify channel responsibilities and escalation points.
- Provide a safe rollback/mitigation checklist to surface with customers.

Scope:
- Multi-tenant and Dedicated deployments (hosted, dedicated, private).
- Incident severities Sev1 (customer-visible outage or quality regression) and Sev2 (significant degradation impacting SLAs).
- Not intended for security incident communications (see "incident-response-security" pages).

Owner and primary contacts:
- Owner: Customer Success (Marisol Vega)
- Primary escalation: CSE Oncall rota (cse-oncall@redwood.ai)
- Engineering escalation: Runtime SRE (eng-sre@redwood.ai)
- Exec escalation: Head of CS (head-cs@redwood.ai)

Channel map and responsibilities (table):
- Primary customer channel: Private Slack DM or sanctioned customer Slack workspace (CSE owns initial comms).
- Incident-wide coordination: #incident-redwood (IC owns timeline & action items).
- Engineering triage: #runtime-triage (SRE/Runtime engineer owns technical diagnosis).
- Billing/FinOps: #billing-escalations (Finance owns cost explanations and credits).
- External status visibility: Status Dashboard & optional customer-facing email (Comms PM owns public post).

Immediate steps for a customer-visible incident (0–10 minutes):
1) Acknowledge: CSE sends initial acknowledgment to customer within SLA window (default 15 minutes for enterprise).
2) Create incident in tracker (Jira/INC-##) and post summary to #incident-redwood with tags: [SEV, AFFECTED_CUSTOMERS, REGION, ROOT_SERVICE].
3) Assign roles: Incident Commander (IC), Communications Lead (CSE), Tech Lead (SRE), Customer Liaison (CSE).
4) Gather quick telemetry: top 3 graphs (requests/sec, error rate, p99 latency) + affected tenant IDs and model variants.

Template library (use the appropriate severity and update cadence). Replace bracketed tokens before sending.

Initial customer acknowledgment (fast template):
"Hi [Customer Name],
Thanks — we see the issue you're reporting for [tenant id / app]. We're investigating now. Our on-call engineering team has been engaged. Expected first update within [15 / 30] minutes. We're treating this as [SEV1/SEV2]. We'll share a short summary and next steps shortly. — [CSE name]"

First technical status update (15–30 mins):
"Status update for [Customer Name] (INC-[id]):
- Impact: [e.g., elevated error rate on generation requests causing 50% failures]
- Scope: [e.g., All US-hosted Dedicated tenants using model X v1.2.3; example tenant ids: T-1234, T-9876]
- What we're doing: [e.g., isolating degraded pool, shifting traffic to compatible variant quantized to q4_0, collecting traces, rolling temporary bypass] 
- Next update: [time + 30 mins]
If you have active customer requests, please forward them to this thread and we'll prioritise. — [CSE name]"

Customer-facing resolution message (post-fix):
"Root cause: [short cause statement].
Mitigation applied: [what we changed to restore service].
Current status: [Service restored/Degraded but mitigated].
Customer impact: [duration and scope].
Actions next: [follow-up items, timeline for permanent fix].
Credits: [if applicable, summary and next steps to apply credits].
If you want a post-incident call, we can schedule a run-through; tell us preferred times. — [CSE name]"

Escalation cadence and when to involve execs:
- Within 60 minutes: If the incident affects >3 enterprise customers or causes sustained SLA violations (error rate >5% and p95 latency >2x target), notify Head of CS and Head of Eng.
- Within 180 minutes: If no short-term mitigation is available or customer business is materially impacted, escalate to Exec Comms and Sales leadership.

Suggested internal Slack snippets (for #incident-redwood). Use code block format for clarity.
"INC-[id] | SEV1 | Impact: [brief]. Affected tenants: [list]. IC: [name]. CSE: [name]. Tech Lead: [name]. Primary mitigation in progress: [action]."

Contact templates for cross-functional owners (email/Slack):
- To Runtime team: "INC-[id] — request: reproduce high-rt error locally with sample request (tenant T-1234). Attached traces/RT: [link]. Priority: P0. Please ack in <10m. — [IC name]"
- To Billing: "INC-[id] — potential bill impact for tenants [T-1234]. Please prepare options for credits and spike analysis. — [CSE name]"

Checklist: safe mitigations to propose to customers (decision tree):
- Is the issue isolated to a single model variant? -> Propose a compatible variant fallback with identical API semantics.
- Is KV cache affecting prefixes? -> Suggest tenant-level cache clear and short rehydrate window.
- Is it network-related in a region? -> Offer regional failover (if configured) or temporary routing to alternative region (note data residency implications).
- If mitigation requires tenant restart: schedule within maintenance window and propose traffic drain procedure.

Communication frequency guidelines:
- SEV1: updates every 15–30 minutes until mitigation, then hourly until RCAs complete.
- SEV2: updates every 30–60 minutes.
- Post-mortem: delivered within 72 hours as a draft; final RCA and action items within 10 business days.

Post-incident follow-up meeting checklist (Customer + Internal):
1) Timeline review and customer impact summary.
2) Walkthrough of telemetry and root cause evidence.
3) Action items and owners with due dates (link to Jira).
4) Compensation/credit decision and approval path.
5) Preventative actions and SLA guardrails to add to QBR.

Short sample Q&A for customer calls (prep sheet):
- Q: Why did this happen? A: We identified a component X regression that, under [workload pattern], caused degraded scheduler decisions. We rolled back and applied a mitigant.
- Q: How can we avoid this? A: We recommend pinning to model variant X.y until the permanent fix and enabling supervised canary for major model upgrades.

Document retention and approvals:
- All outgoing customer messages related to SEV1 incidents must be reviewed by Communications Lead or Head of CS when possible.
- Save all conversations in the incident timeline and link to the customer's record in CRM with tags: incident, outage, credit_pending.

Appendix: Quick copy-paste snippets (use verbatim and fill tokens)
- Short public status page blurb: "Investigating: We are aware of increased errors for text-generation requests in US region. Engineers are actively investigating. No ETA yet. — Redwood Engineering"
- Customer opt-in for call: "We can schedule a 30-minute technical call to review impact and mitigation. Are you available [date/time options]?"

References and related pages:
- Incident comms standards (internal)
- Postmortem template and RCA tracker
- Dedicated tenant cutover safety net (see related pages)

Revision notes:
- 2027-08-18: Initial draft and CSE oncall validated rapid-ack template.
- 2027-11-05: Added KV-cache mitigation decision tree after two incidents.
- 2028-01-12: Finalized exec escalation thresholds and added billing coordination templates.

End of document.
